question_text: Find the equation of the circle passing through (3,4) and with centre at (−3,4).

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, SENIOR INTER MATHS-2B (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.103 — the Bullet Model Paper, under "Q1 & 2: CIRCLES". It is NOT worked in the numbered VSAQ chapter, whose nearest answers are 108.1 (centre at the origin) and 108.2 (a different centre and point), so it is authored here as an extra. Its SECTION follows the paper slot: the Bullet Model Paper places it at Q1/Q2, which is Section A, so it is a VSAQ. No appearance tag is printed beside it. There is no printed 2-mark split in this book to pattern it on, so it splits the answer at its one natural break. Star rank: the book’s VSAQ chapter table (book p.76) and its VSAQ hit list header (book p.11) both give the CIRCLE VSAQ chapter ★★★, but the chapter header printed on book p.77 shows only ★★. Paper position: Maths-2B Section A runs Q1-Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory; Circle holds Q1 and Q2. Every number was re-derived and the book is correct: r = 6 and the circle is x² + y² + 6x − 8y − 11 = 0. insider_note: The centre and the given point share the same y-coordinate, so the radius is just the horizontal gap — reading that off saves the whole distance calculation.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find the radius
steps.margin_note: One mark. Both points are at y = 4, so the y part of the distance is zero.
steps.memory_tip: Same y-coordinate means the distance is the difference of the x-coordinates.
lines: Centre C = (−3, 4), point on the circle P = (3, 4)
steps.why: The radius is the distance from the centre to any point on the circle. Here the two points lie on the same horizontal line, so the distance is simply 3 − (−3) = 6.
common_mistakes: Writing (3 + 3) as 0 by subtracting instead of adding.
Using the centre as the point on the circle.

steps.label: Write the equation
lines: Circle with centre (−3, 4) and radius 6 is
steps.why: Expanding the centre-radius form gives the general equation, and the constant is 9 + 16 − 36 = −11. A check: putting (3, 4) in gives 9 + 16 + 18 − 32 − 11 = 0.
